mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 2 Series M235i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 2 Series M235i engine replacement typically costs between £2,400 and £4,500 depending on the condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt) and the specific engine code. Used engines start from around £1,600, reconditioned units from £2,400, and fully rebuilt engines with a 12-month warranty from £2,800. Labour for supply and fit adds approximately £800-£1,500 depending on the workshop. Main dealer replacement costs can exceed £5,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of charge pipe failure in a BMW 2 Series M235i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common symptom is a sudden loss of power accompanied by a "drivetrain malfunction" warning on the iDrive screen. You may also hear a loud whooshing noise from the engine bay under acceleration. The N55's plastic charge pipe is notoriously prone to failure under boost pressure. If this happens, the car will enter limp mode to protect the engine.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 2 Series M235i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and the extent of the damage. For a 2014-2016 M235i worth £10,000-£18,000, a reconditioned engine at £2,400-£3,400 is often worthwhile if you plan to keep the car. For F44 Gran Coupe models (2020+) worth £20,000-£30,000, replacement is almost always justified. If the car is worth under £5,000, a used engine or repair may be more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 2 Series M235i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 2 Series M235i engine replacement takes 3-5 working days from order to completion, assuming the engine is in stock. Supply-only orders are usually dispatched within 1-2 working days. Supply and fit through our specialist network typically takes 3-5 days, including delivery, fitting, and ECU calibration.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the M235i and the M240i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW M235i (2014-2016) uses the N55 3.0-litre inline-six producing 326hp, while the M240i (2017-2021) uses the newer B58 3.0-litre inline-six producing 340hp. The M240i replaced the M235i in the F22/F23 generation. The M235i name was later revived for the F44 Gran Coupe (2019-2024) with a B48 2.0-litre four-cylinder producing 306hp.

mainEntity.name: Will a replacement BMW 2 Series M235i engine pass the MoT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all engines supplied through EnginesMarket are MoT emissions compliant. Rebuilt and reconditioned engines are tested to ensure they meet the original emissions standards for the vehicle's year. For M235i models with OPF (Otto Particulate Filter), compliance is confirmed before dispatch.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 2 Series M235i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 2 Series M235i arrived in 2014 as the first M Performance model in the 2 Series range, powered by BMW's acclaimed N55 3.0-litre inline-six turbo engine producing 326hp. In 2020, the M235i badge was revived for the F44 Gran Coupe, now powered by a high-output 2.0-litre B48 four-cylinder turbo producing 306hp - a very different character but carrying the same M Performance mantle.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 2 Series M235i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 2 Series M235i has been powered by two very different engines: the N55 3.0-litre inline-six (2014-2016) and the B48 2.0-litre four-cylinder (2019-2024). The N55 is renowned for its character but suffers from plastic charge pipe failure and oil starvation under hard use. The B48 is more modern but has its own plastic component weaknesses. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Charge Pipe Failure - Why the BMW 2 Series M235i N55 Engine Loses Boost
problems.rootCause: The N55's plastic charge pipe is notoriously prone to failure under boost pressure. The pipe connects the turbocharger to the intercooler and can crack or blow off completely, resulting in a sudden loss of boost, reduced power, and a drivetrain malfunction warning. This is widely considered a design flaw in the N55 engine.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective; upgraded unit eliminates future failure

problems.recommendation: Charge pipe failure is a well-known weakness on the N55 M235i. Upgrading to an aluminium charge pipe is a relatively inexpensive fix that prevents future failure. If the engine has suffered catastrophic boost-related damage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N55B30 BMW 2 Series M235i engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Starvation - BMW 2 Series M235i N55 Engine Under Hard Cornering
problems.typicalFailureMileage: Track use or sustained hard driving - can occur at any mileage
problems.rootCause: It's well documented that the N55 engine found in the M235i is prone to oil starvation issues when pushed hard on the road and even more so when used on track. Under sustained high-G cornering, oil can surge away from the oil pickup, leading to momentary oil pressure loss and potential bearing damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect oil pump, bearings, oil pressure
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil pressure warning appears

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip, inspect, replace bearings and damaged components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation has caused bearing failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a typical £10,000-£18,000 M235i, a baffled sump is a worthwhile preventative investment if you track the car. Full engine replacement is rarely needed unless oil starvation has caused catastrophic bearing failure.
problems.recommendation: If you track your M235i or drive it hard on B-roads, a baffled sump is a wise investment. If you've experienced an oil pressure warning, have the engine inspected immediately - bearing damage can escalate quickly.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW 2 Series M235i engine diagnostics

problems.h4: Plastic Oil Filter Housing Cracking - BMW 2 Series M235i B48 Gran Coupe Coolant and Oil Leaks
problems.rootCause: The B48 oil filter housing is made of plastic and can crack over time, creating coolant or oil leaks. Because the housing is located underneath the intake manifold, the manifold must be removed to access it, making repairs labour-intensive.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, replace housing and gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective; upgraded units typically don't fail again

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Pressure test, inspect for additional leaks

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a typical £20,000-£30,000 M235i Gran Coupe, oil filter housing replacement is a worthwhile repair. Full engine replacement is rarely needed for this failure alone.
problems.recommendation: Oil filter housing cracking is a known issue on B48 engines. Regularly check for coolant or oil puddles under the car. Replacing the housing with an upgraded unit typically solves the problem permanently.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW 2 Series M235i oil filter housing repair

problems.h4: Wastegate Rattle - BMW 2 Series M235i B48 Turbocharger Issues
problems.affectedModels: BMW 2 Series M235i (B48A20O1, B48A20O0, all years)
problems.rootCause: The BMW M235i turbo engine suffers from wastegate issues which become progressively worse with normal driving and especially with harsh driving conditions. "Wastegate rattle" or "turbo rattle" is a result of excessive movement between the wastegate and the wastegate seat.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if turbo core is undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip, clean, rebuild turbo with new actuator
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if turbo has shaft play
Required if turbo core is damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a typical £20,000-£30,000 M235i Gran Coupe, turbo repairs are worthwhile. Full engine replacement is rarely needed for turbo failure alone.
problems.recommendation: Wastegate rattle is common on B48 M235i engines. Replace the actuator early to prevent further turbo wear. If the turbo has already failed, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with upgraded components may be the most cost-effective solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare BMW 2 Series M235i turbo repair costs
